status.label: Broader than Window Hopper's window scope
status.detail: The request combines tab enumeration and activation across Explorer, browsers, and Terminal, whose tabs are owned by different applications.

next_action.label: Post scope decision
next_action.reason: A universal cross-application tab switcher is a product-direction decision rather than a bounded Window Hopper fix.

comment.body: Window Hopper currently operates on top-level application windows. The requested tabs belong to different applications—Explorer, browsers, and Terminal—and do not share one universal enumeration and activation contract, so system-wide tab support is substantially broader than extending the existing window list. This should not enter implementation as one generic Window Hopper change; maintainers would first need to select a specific supported application/API or define a separate app-integration model. In the meantime, each application's native tab shortcut remains the reliable path.

judgment.rationale: The proposal is a cross-application product expansion without a selected integration contract, not a currently bounded defect or design task.
evidence: The request asks Window Hopper to switch tabs in Explorer, Edge, Chrome, Firefox, and Terminal.
The existing feature is described as switching separate windows within one application.
No single priority application or tab-enumeration interface is selected.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a substantive scope response explaining why maintainers must choose an application/API strategy before implementation.
